articles.title: How to Reduce Flutter App Size: 12 Proven Techniques
articles.excerpt: How to Reduce Flutter App Size: 12 Proven Techniques That Actually Work You've built a beautiful Flutter app. It runs flawlessly. Then you check the APK size: 47MB. For a todo app. Meanwhile, a compar…
articles.body: How to Reduce Flutter App Size: 12 Proven Techniques That Actually Work You've built a beautiful Flutter app. It runs flawlessly. Then you check the APK size: 47MB . For a todo app. Meanwhile, a comparable native app ships at 12MB. What gives — and more importantly, how do you fix it? Flutter apps carry inherent weight: the Dart VM/engine (~4-7MB per ABI), ICU internationalization data, and the framework itself. A minimal release APK starts around 15-20MB before you write a single line of code. But most bloated Flutter apps I audit aren't victims of the engine — they're victims of avoidable mistakes: unoptimized assets, unused dependencies, and debug-era build configs shipped to production. Here are 12 techniques I use to slim down production Flutter apps, ordered roughly by impact. 1.

articles.body: This tutorial was written with AI assistance from the project's official documentation. Verification status is stated at the end of the article. What Whoogle Search does and what it needs Whoogle Search is a self-hosted metasearch front end that fetches Google results server-side and serves them without ads, JavaScript, AMP links, cookies, or IP tracking. Your browser talks only to your instance; the instance talks to Google. It supports Tor and HTTP/SOCKS proxies, custom bangs, JSON output, and basic auth. Important status note: the upstream README states that Whoogle reached end of life on 24 Jul 2026. Google shut down the non-JavaScript search path Whoogle relied on, and the project is no longer maintained.

articles.body: Darwin-180B-RSI Tops Legal Reasoning Benchmarks With Zero Legal Training Data — Here's the Technical Story TL;DR: VIDRAFT's Darwin-180B-RSI is a 180-billion-parameter reasoning model that achieved #1 on two Hugging Face-certified legal benchmarks (LEXam and LEXam-hard) without being trained on any legal data. The model uses diagnostics-driven model merging and a Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) loop powered by a novel Zero-Token Confidence (ZTC) mechanism — modifying only 0.02% of total parameters in the process. If you're building reasoning systems or evaluating frontier models, this result challenges core assumptions about domain specialization.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998:  Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. It was just one piece, but the foundation of something much larger.
articles.body: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station.

articles.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
articles.excerpt: Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing the lunar environment may suffer irreversible damage if things move too fast.
articles.body: Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment.

articles.body: Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago.
